This is a list of the members of the '''1925 [[Seanad Éireann (Irish Free State)|Seanad Éireann]]''', the [[upper house]] of the [[Oireachtas of the Irish Free State|Oireachtas]] (legislature) of the [[Irish Free State]]. These [[Senate|Senator]]s were elected or appointed in 1922, and also elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Free State Seanad election]].

==Composition of the 1925 Seanad==
The Free State Seanad was elected in stages and thus considered to be in permanent session. However, as a gesture of continuity with its Free State predecessor, the first [[Seanad Éireann|Seanad elected after 1937]] is numbered as the "Second Seanad". The Free State Senate, despite the occurrence of three senatorial elections before its abolition, is considered to have been a single 'Seanad' for the duration of its existence and is thus referred for that whole period as the "First Seanad".

There were a total of 60 seats in the Free State Seanad. In 1925, 19 Senators were elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Free State Seanad election]], which was the only Seanad [[Universal suffrage|popular election]].

This is a list of the members of the '''1925 [[Seanad Éireann (Irish Free State)|Seanad Éireann]]''', the [[upper house]] of the [[Oireachtas of the Irish Free State|Oireachtas]] (legislature) of the [[Irish Free State]]. These [[Senate|Senator]]s were elected or appointed in 1922, and also elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Free State Seanad election]].

==Composition of the 1925 Seanad==
The Free State Seanad was elected in stages and thus considered to be in permanent session. However, as a gesture of continuity with its Free State predecessor, the first [[Seanad Éireann|Seanad elected after 1937]] is numbered as the "Second Seanad". The Free State Senate, despite the occurrence of three senatorial elections before its abolition, is considered to have been a single 'Seanad' for the duration of its existence and is thus referred for that whole period as the "First Seanad".

There were a total of 60 seats in the Free State Seanad. In 1925, 19 Senators were elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Free State Seanad election]], which was the only Seanad [[Universal suffrage|popular election]].

This is a list of the members of the '''1925 [[Seanad Éireann (Irish Free State)|Seanad Éireann]]''', the [[upper house]] of the [[Oireachtas of the Irish Free State|Oireachtas]] (legislature) of the [[Irish Free State]]. These [[Senate|Senator]]s were elected or appointed in 1922, and also elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Free State Seanad election]].

==Composition of the 1925 Seanad==
The Free State Seanad was elected in stages and thus considered to be in permanent session. However, as a gesture of continuity with its Free State predecessor, the first [[Seanad Éireann|Seanad elected after 1937]] is numbered as the "Second Seanad". The Free State Senate, despite the occurrence of three senatorial elections before its abolition, is considered to have been a single 'Seanad' for the duration of its existence and is thus referred for that whole period as the "First Seanad".

There were a total of 60 seats in the Free State Seanad. In 1925, 19 Senators were elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Free State Seanad election]], which was the only Seanad [[Universal suffrage|popular election]]. In 1922, 35 Senators had been elected by [[Dáil Éireann (Irish Free State)|Dáil Éireann]], and 25 had been nominated by the [[President of the Executive Council of the Irish Free State|President of the Executive Council]], [[W. T. Cosgrave]].

This is a list of the members of the '''1925 [[Seanad Éireann (Irish Free State)|Seanad Éireann]]''', the [[upper house]] of the [[Oireachtas of the Irish Free State|Oireachtas]] (legislature) of the [[Irish Free State]]. These [[Senate|Senator]]s were elected or appointed in 1922, and also elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Free State Seanad election]].

==Composition of the 1925 Seanad==
The Free State Seanad was elected in stages and thus considered to be in permanent session. However, as a gesture of continuity with its Free State predecessor, the first [[Seanad Éireann|Seanad elected after 1937]] is numbered as the "Second Seanad". The Free State Senate, despite the occurrence of three senatorial elections before its abolition, is considered to have been a single 'Seanad' for the duration of its existence and is thus referred for that whole period as the "First Seanad".

There were a total of 60 seats in the Free State Seanad. In 1925, 19 Senators were elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Free State Seanad election]], which was the only Seanad [[Universal suffrage|popular election]]. In 1922, 35 Senators had been elected by [[Dáil Éireann (Irish Free State)|Dáil Éireann]], and 25 had been nominated by the [[President of the Executive Council of the Irish Free State|President of the Executive Council]], [[W. T. Cosgrave]].

This is a list of the members of the '''1925 [[Seanad Éireann (Irish Free State)|Seanad Éireann]]''', the [[upper house]] of the [[Oireachtas of the Irish Free State|Oireachtas]] (legislature) of the [[Irish Free State]]. These [[Senate|Senator]]s were elected or appointed in 1922, and also elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Free State Seanad election]].

==Composition of the 1925 Seanad==
The Free State Seanad was elected in stages and thus considered to be in permanent session. However, as a gesture of continuity with its Free State predecessor, the first [[Seanad Éireann|Seanad elected after 1937]] is numbered as the "Second Seanad". The Free State Senate, despite the occurrence of three senatorial elections before its abolition, is considered to have been a single 'Seanad' for the duration of its existence and is thus referred for that whole period as the "First Seanad".

There were a total of 60 seats in the Free State Seanad. In 1925, 19 Senators were elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Free State Seanad election]], which was the only Seanad [[Universal suffrage|popular election]]. In 1922, 35 Senators had been elected by [[Dáil Éireann (Irish Free State)|Dáil Éireann]], and 25 had been nominated by the [[President of the Executive Council of the Irish Free State|President of the Executive Council]], [[W. T. Cosgrave]].

This is a list of the members of the '''1925 [[Seanad Éireann (Irish Free State)|Seanad Éireann]]''', the [[upper house]] of the [[Oireachtas of the Irish Free State|Oireachtas]] (legislature) of the [[Irish Free State]]. These [[Senate|Senator]]s were elected or appointed in 1922, and also elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Free State Seanad election]].

==Composition of the 1925 Seanad==
The Free State Seanad was elected in stages and thus considered to be in permanent session. However, as a gesture of continuity with its Free State predecessor, the first [[Seanad Éireann|Seanad elected after 1937]] is numbered as the "Second Seanad". The Free State Senate, despite the occurrence of three senatorial elections before its abolition, is considered to have been a single 'Seanad' for the duration of its existence and is thus referred for that whole period as the "First Seanad".

There were a total of 60 seats in the Free State Seanad. In 1925, 19 Senators were elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Free State Seanad election]], which was the only Seanad [[Universal suffrage|popular election]]. In 1922, 35 Senators had been elected by [[Dáil Éireann (Irish Free State)|Dáil Éireann]], and 25 had been nominated by the [[President of the Executive Council of the Irish Free State|President of the Executive Council]], [[W. T. Cosgrave]].

This is a list of the members of the '''1925 [[Seanad Éireann (Irish Free State)|Seanad Éireann]]''', the [[upper house]] of the [[Oireachtas of the Irish Free State|Oireachtas]] (legislature) of the [[Irish Free State]]. These [[Senate|Senator]]s were elected or appointed in 1922, and also elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Free State Seanad election]].

==Composition of the 1925 Seanad==
The Free State Seanad was elected in stages and thus considered to be in permanent session. However, as a gesture of continuity with its Free State predecessor, the first [[Seanad Éireann|Seanad elected after 1937]] is numbered as the "Second Seanad". The Free State Senate, despite the occurrence of three senatorial elections before its abolition, is considered to have been a single 'Seanad' for the duration of its existence and is thus referred for that whole period as the "First Seanad".

There were a total of 60 seats in the Free State Seanad. In 1925, 19 Senators were elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Free State Seanad election]], which was the only Seanad [[Universal suffrage|popular election]]. In 1922, 35 Senators had been elected by [[Dáil Éireann (Irish Free State)|Dáil Éireann]], and 25 had been nominated by the [[President of the Executive Council of the Irish Free State|President of the Executive Council]], [[W. T. Cosgrave]].

This is a list of the members of the '''1925 [[Seanad Éireann (Irish Free State)|Seanad Éireann]]''', the [[upper house]] of the [[Oireachtas of the Irish Free State|Oireachtas]] (legislature) of the [[Irish Free State]]. These [[Senate|Senator]]s were elected or appointed in 1922, and also elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Free State Seanad election]].

==Composition of the 1925 Seanad==
The Free State Seanad was elected in stages and thus considered to be in permanent session. However, as a gesture of continuity with its Free State predecessor, the first [[Seanad Éireann|Seanad elected after 1937]] is numbered as the "Second Seanad". The Free State Senate, despite the occurrence of five senatorial elections before its abolition, is considered to have been a single 'Seanad' for the duration of its existence and is thus referred for that whole period as the "First Seanad".

There were a total of 60 seats in the Free State Seanad. 19 Senators were elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Free State Seanad election]], which was the only Seanad [[Universal suffrage|popular election]]. In 1922, 35 Senators had been elected by [[Dáil Éireann (Irish Free State)|Dáil Éireann]], and 25 had been nominated by the [[President of the Executive Council of the Irish Free State|President of the Executive Council]], [[W. T. Cosgrave]].

This is a list of the members of the '''1925 [[Seanad Éireann (Irish Free State)|Seanad Éireann]]''', the [[upper house]] of the [[Oireachtas of the Irish Free State|Oireachtas]] (legislature) of the [[Irish Free State]]. These [[Senate|Senator]]s were elected or appointed in 1922, and also elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Seanad election]].

==Composition of the 1925 Seanad==
The Free State Seanad was elected in stages and thus considered to be in permanent session. However, as a gesture of continuity with its Free State predecessor, the first [[Seanad Éireann|Seanad elected after 1937]] is numbered as the "Second Seanad". The Free State Senate, despite the occurrence of five senatorial elections before its abolition, is considered to have been a single 'Seanad' for the duration of its existence and is thus referred for that whole period as the "First Seanad".

There were a total of 60 seats in the Free State Seanad. 19 Senators were elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Free State Seanad election]], which was the only Seanad [[Universal suffrage|popular election]]. In 1922, 35 Senators had been elected by [[Dáil Éireann (Irish Free State)|Dáil Éireann]], and 25 had been nominated by the [[President of the Executive Council of the Irish Free State|President of the Executive Council]], [[W. T. Cosgrave]].

This is a list of the members of the '''1925 [[Seanad Éireann (Irish Free State)|Seanad Éireann]]''', the [[upper house]] of the [[Oireachtas of the Irish Free State|Oireachtas]] (legislature) of the [[Irish Free State]]. These [[Senate|Senator]]s were elected or appointed in 1922, and also elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Seanad election]].

==Composition of the 1925 Seanad==
The Free State Seanad was elected in stages and thus considered to be in permanent session. However, as a gesture of continuity with its Free State predecessor, the first [[Seanad Éireann|Seanad elected after 1937]] is numbered as the "Second Seanad". The Free State Senate, despite the occurrence of five senatorial elections before its abolition, is considered to have been a single 'Seanad' for the duration of its existence and is thus referred for that whole period as the "First Seanad".

There were a total of 60 seats in the Free State Seanad. 19 Senators were elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Free State Seanad election]], which was the only Seanad [[Universal suffrage|popular election]]. In 1922, 35 Senators had been elected by [[Dáil Éireann (Irish Free State)|Dáil Éireann]], and 25 had been nominated by the [[President of the Executive Council of the Irish Free State|President of the Executive Council]], [[W. T. Cosgrave]].

This is a list of the members of the '''1925 [[Seanad Éireann (Irish Free State)|Seanad Éireann]]''', the [[upper house]] of the [[Oireachtas of the Irish Free State|Oireachtas]] (legislature) of the [[Irish Free State]]. These [[Senate|Senator]]s were elected or appointed in 1922, and also elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Seanad election]].

==Composition of the 1925 Seanad==
The Free State Seanad was elected in stages and thus considered to be in permanent session. However, as a gesture of continuity with its Free State predecessor, the first [[Seanad Éireann|Seanad elected after 1937]] is numbered as the "Second Seanad". The Free State Senate, despite the occurrence of five senatorial elections before its abolition, is considered to have been a single 'Seanad' for the duration of its existence and is thus referred for that whole period as the "First Seanad".

There were a total of 60 seats in the Free State Seanad. 19 Senators were elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Free State Seanad election]], which was the only Seanad [[Universal suffrage|popular election]]. In 1922, 35 Senators had been elected by [[Dáil Éireann (Irish Free State)|Dáil Éireann]], and 25 had been nominated by the [[President of the Executive Council of the Irish Free State|President of the Executive Council]], [[W. T. Cosgrave]].

This is a list of the members of the '''1925 [[Seanad Éireann (Irish Free State)|Seanad Éireann]]''', the [[upper house]] of the [[Oireachtas of the Irish Free State|Oireachtas]] (legislature) of the [[Irish Free State]]. These [[Senate|Senator]]s were elected or appointed in 1922, and also elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Seanad election]].

==Composition of the 1925 Seanad==
The Free State Seanad was elected in stages and thus considered to be in permanent session. However, as a gesture of continuity with its Free State predecessor, the first [[Seanad Éireann|Seanad elected after 1937]] is numbered as the "Second Seanad". The Free State Senate, despite the occurrence of five senatorial elections before its abolition, is considered to have been a single 'Seanad' for the duration of its existence and is thus referred for that whole period as the "First Seanad".

There were a total of 60 seats in the Free State Seanad. 19 Senators were elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Free State Seanad election]], which was the only Seanad [[Universal suffrage|popular election]]. In 1922, 35 Senators had been elected by [[Dáil Éireann (Irish Free State)|Dáil Éireann]], and 25 had been nominated by the [[President of the Executive Council of the Irish Free State|President of the Executive Council]], [[W. T. Cosgrave]].

This is a list of the members of the '''1925 [[Seanad Éireann (Irish Free State)|Seanad Éireann]]''', the [[upper house]] of the [[Oireachtas of the Irish Free State|Oireachtas]] (legislature) of the [[Irish Free State]]. These [[Senate|Senator]]s were elected or appointed in 1922, and also elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Seanad election]].

==Composition of the 1925 Seanad==
The Free State Seanad was elected in stages and thus considered to be in permanent session. However, as a gesture of continuity with its Free State predecessor, the first [[Seanad Éireann|Seanad elected after 1937]] is numbered as the "Second Seanad". The Free State Senate, despite the occurrence of five senatorial elections before its abolition, is considered to have been a single 'Seanad' for the duration of its existence and is thus referred for that whole period as the "First Seanad".

There were a total of 60 seats in the Free State Seanad. 19 Senators were elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Free State Seanad election]], which was the only Seanad [[Universal suffrage|popular election]]. In 1922, 35 Senators had been elected by [[Dáil Éireann (Irish Free State)|Dáil Éireann]], and 25 had been nominated by the [[President of the Executive Council of the Irish Free State|President of the Executive Council]], [[W. T. Cosgrave]].

This is a list of the members of the '''1925 [[Seanad Éireann (Irish Free State)|Seanad Éireann]]''', the [[upper house]] of the [[Oireachtas of the Irish Free State|Oireachtas]] (legislature) of the [[Irish Free State]]. These [[Senate|Senator]]s were elected or appointed in 1922, and also elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Seanad election]].

==Composition of the 1925 Seanad==
The Free State Seanad was elected in stages and thus considered to be in permanent session. However, as a gesture of continuity with its Free State predecessor, the first [[Seanad Éireann|Seanad elected after 1937]] is numbered as the "Second Seanad". The Free State Senate, despite the occurrence of five senatorial elections before its abolition, is considered to have been a single 'Seanad' for the duration of its existence and is thus referred for that whole period as the "First Seanad".

There were a total of 60 seats in the Free State Seanad. 19 Senators were elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Free State Seanad election]], which was the only Seanad [[Universal suffrage|popular election]]. In 1922, 35 Senators had been elected by [[Dáil Éireann (Irish Free State)|Dáil Éireann]], and 25 had been nominated by the [[President of the Executive Council of the Irish Free State|President of the Executive Council]], [[W. T. Cosgrave]].

This is a list of the members of the '''1925 [[Seanad Éireann (Irish Free State)|Seanad Éireann]]''', the [[upper house]] of the [[Oireachtas of the Irish Free State|Oireachtas]] (legislature) of the [[Irish Free State]]. These [[Senate|Senator]]s were elected or appointed in 1922, and also elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Seanad election]].

==Composition of the 1925 Seanad==
The Free State Seanad was elected in stages and thus considered to be in permanent session. However, as a gesture of continuity with its Free State predecessor, the first [[Seanad Éireann|Seanad elected after 1937]] is numbered as the "Second Seanad". The Free State Senate, despite the occurrence of five senatorial elections before its abolition, is considered to have been a single 'Seanad' for the duration of its existence and is thus referred for that whole period as the "First Seanad".

There were a total of 60 seats in the Free State Seanad. 19 Senators were elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Free State Seanad election]], which was the only Seanad [[Universal suffrage|popular election]]. In 1922, 35 Senators had been elected by [[Dáil Éireann (Irish Free State)|Dáil Éireann]], and 25 had been nominated by the [[President of the Executive Council of the Irish Free State|President of the Executive Council]], [[W. T. Cosgrave]].

This is a list of the members of the '''1925 [[Seanad Éireann (Irish Free State)|Seanad Éireann]]''', the [[upper house]] of the [[Oireachtas of the Irish Free State|Oireachtas]] (legislature) of the [[Irish Free State]]. These [[Senate|Senator]]s were elected or appointed in 1922, and also elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Seanad election]].

==Composition of the 1925 Seanad==
The Free State Seanad was elected in stages and thus considered to be in permanent session. However, as a gesture of continuity with its Free State predecessor, the first [[Seanad Éireann|Seanad elected after 1937]] is numbered as the "Second Seanad". The Free State Senate, despite the occurrence of five senatorial elections before its abolition, is considered to have been a single 'Seanad' for the duration of its existence and is thus referred for that whole period as the "First Seanad".

There were a total of 60 seats in the Free State Seanad. 19 Senators were elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Free State Seanad election]], which was the only Seanad [[Universal suffrage|popular election]]. In 1922, 35 Senators had been elected by [[Dáil Éireann (Irish Free State)|Dáil Éireann]], and 25 had been nominated by the [[President of the Executive Council of the Irish Free State|President of the Executive Council]], [[W. T. Cosgrave]].

This is a list of the members of the '''1925 [[Seanad Éireann (Irish Free State)|Seanad Éireann]]''', the [[upper house]] of the [[Oireachtas of the Irish Free State|Oireachtas]] (legislature) of the [[Irish Free State]]. These [[Senate|Senator]]s were elected or appointed in 1922, and also elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Seanad election]].

==Composition of the 1925 Seanad==
The Free State Seanad was elected in stages and thus considered to be in permanent session. However, as a gesture of continuity with its Free State predecessor, the first [[Seanad Éireann|Seanad elected after 1937]] is numbered as the "Second Seanad". The Free State Senate, despite the occurrence of five senatorial elections before its abolition, is considered to have been a single 'Seanad' for the duration of its existence and is thus referred for that whole period as the "First Seanad".

There were a total of 60 seats in the Free State Seanad. 19 Senators were elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Free State Seanad election]], which was the only Seanad [[Universal suffrage|popular election]]. In 1922, 35 Senators had been elected by [[Dáil Éireann (Irish Free State)|Dáil Éireann]], and 25 had been nominated by the [[President of the Executive Council of the Irish Free State|President of the Executive Council]], [[W. T. Cosgrave]].

This is a list of the members of the '''1925 [[Seanad Éireann (Irish Free State)|Seanad Éireann]]''', the [[upper house]] of the [[Oireachtas of the Irish Free State|Oireachtas]] (legislature) of the [[Irish Free State]]. These [[Senate|Senator]]s were elected or appointed in 1922, and also elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Seanad election]].

==Composition of the 1925 Seanad==
The Free State Seanad was elected in stages and thus considered to be in permanent session. However, as a gesture of continuity with its Free State predecessor, the first [[Seanad Éireann|Seanad elected after 1937]] is numbered as the "Second Seanad". The Free State Senate, despite the occurrence of five senatorial elections before its abolition, is considered to have been a single 'Seanad' for the duration of its existence and is thus referred for that whole period as the "First Seanad".

There were a total of 60 seats in the Free State Seanad. 19 Senators were elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Free State Seanad election]], which was the only Seanad [[Universal suffrage|popular election]]. In 1922, 35 Senators had been elected by [[Dáil Éireann (Irish Free State)|Dáil Éireann]], and 25 had been nominated by the [[President of the Executive Council of the Irish Free State|President of the Executive Council]], [[W. T. Cosgrave]].

This is a list of the members of the '''1925 [[Seanad Éireann (Irish Free State)|Seanad Éireann]]''', the [[upper house]] of the [[Oireachtas of the Irish Free State|Oireachtas]] (legislature) of the [[Irish Free State]]. These [[Senate|Senator]]s were elected or appointed in 1922, and also elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Seanad election]].

==Composition of the 1925 Seanad==
The Free State Seanad was elected in stages and thus considered to be in permanent session. However, as a gesture of continuity with its Free State predecessor, the first [[Seanad Éireann|Seanad elected after 1937]] is numbered as the "Second Seanad". The Free State Senate, despite the occurrence of five senatorial elections before its abolition, is considered to have been a single 'Seanad' for the duration of its existence and is thus referred for that whole period as the "First Seanad".

There were a total of 60 seats in the Free State Seanad. 19 Senators were elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Free State Seanad election]], which was the only Seanad [[Universal suffrage|popular election]]. In 1922, 35 Senators had been elected by [[Dáil Éireann (Irish Free State)|Dáil Éireann]], and 25 had been nominated by the [[President of the Executive Council of the Irish Free State|President of the Executive Council]], [[W. T. Cosgrave]].

This is a list of the members of the '''1925 [[Seanad Éireann (Irish Free State)|Seanad Éireann]]''', the [[upper house]] of the [[Oireachtas of the Irish Free State|Oireachtas]] (legislature) of the [[Irish Free State]]. These [[Senate|Senator]]s were elected or appointed in 1922, and also elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Seanad election]].

==Composition of the 1925 Seanad==
The Free State Seanad was elected in stages and thus considered to be in permanent session. However, as a gesture of continuity with its Free State predecessor, the first [[Seanad Éireann|Seanad elected after 1937]] is numbered as the "Second Seanad". The Free State Senate, despite the occurrence of five senatorial elections before its abolition, is considered to have been a single 'Seanad' for the duration of its existence and is thus referred for that whole period as the "First Seanad".

There were a total of 60 seats in the Free State Seanad. 19 Senators were elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Free State Seanad election]], which was the only Seanad [[Universal suffrage|popular election]]. In 1922, 35 Senators had been elected by [[Dáil Éireann (Irish Free State)|Dáil Éireann]], and 25 had been nominated by the [[President of the Executive Council of the Irish Free State|President of the Executive Council]], [[W. T. Cosgrave]].

This is a list of the members of the '''1925 [[Seanad Éireann (Irish Free State)|Seanad Éireann]]''', the [[upper house]] of the [[Oireachtas of the Irish Free State|Oireachtas]] (legislature) of the [[Irish Free State]]. These [[Senate|Senator]]s were elected or appointed in 1922, and also elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Seanad election]].

==Composition of the 1925 Seanad==
The Free State Seanad was elected in stages and thus considered to be in permanent session. However, as a gesture of continuity with its Free State predecessor, the first [[Seanad Éireann|Seanad elected after 1937]] is numbered as the "Second Seanad". The Free State Senate, despite the occurrence of five senatorial elections before its abolition, is considered to have been a single 'Seanad' for the duration of its existence and is thus referred for that whole period as the "First Seanad".

There were a total of 60 seats in the Free State Seanad. 19 Senators were elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Free State Seanad election]], which was the only Seanad [[Universal suffrage|popular election]]. In 1922, 35 Senators had been elected by [[Dáil Éireann (Irish Free State)|Dáil Éireann]], and 25 had been nominated by the [[President of the Executive Council of the Irish Free State|President of the Executive Council]], [[W. T. Cosgrave]].

This is a list of the members of the '''1925 [[Seanad Éireann (Irish Free State)|Seanad Éireann]]''', the [[upper house]] of the [[Oireachtas of the Irish Free State|Oireachtas]] (legislature) of the [[Irish Free State]]. These [[Senate|Senator]]s were elected or appointed in 1922, and also elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Seanad election]].

==Composition of the 1925 Seanad==
The Free State Seanad was elected in stages and thus considered to be in permanent session. However, as a gesture of continuity with its Free State predecessor, the first [[Seanad Éireann|Seanad elected after 1937]] is numbered as the "Second Seanad". The Free State Senate, despite the occurrence of five senatorial elections before its abolition, is considered to have been a single 'Seanad' for the duration of its existence and is thus referred for that whole period as the "First Seanad".

There were a total of 60 seats in the Free State Seanad. 19 Senators were elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Free State Seanad election]], which was the only Seanad [[Universal suffrage|popular election]]. In 1922, 35 Senators had been elected by [[Dáil Éireann (Irish Free State)|Dáil Éireann]], and 25 had been nominated by the [[President of the Executive Council of the Irish Free State|President of the Executive Council]], [[W. T. Cosgrave]].

This is a list of the members of the '''1925 [[Seanad Éireann (Irish Free State)|Seanad Éireann]]''', the [[upper house]] of the [[Oireachtas of the Irish Free State|Oireachtas]] (legislature) of the [[Irish Free State]]. These [[Senate|Senator]]s were elected or appointed in 1922, and also elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Seanad election]].

==Composition of the 1925 Seanad==
The Free State Seanad was elected in stages and thus considered to be in permanent session. However, as a gesture of continuity with its Free State predecessor, the first [[Seanad Éireann|Seanad elected after 1937]] is numbered as the "Second Seanad". The Free State Senate, despite the occurrence of five senatorial elections before its abolition, is considered to have been a single 'Seanad' for the duration of its existence and is thus referred for that whole period as the "First Seanad".

There were a total of 60 seats in the Free State Seanad. 19 Senators were elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Free State Seanad election]], which was the only Seanad [[Universal suffrage|popular election]]. In 1922, 35 Senators had been elected by [[Dáil Éireann (Irish Free State)|Dáil Éireann]], and 25 had been nominated by the [[President of the Executive Council of the Irish Free State|President of the Executive Council]], [[W. T. Cosgrave]].

This is a list of the members of the '''1925 [[Seanad Éireann (Irish Free State)|Seanad Éireann]]''', the [[upper house]] of the [[Oireachtas of the Irish Free State|Oireachtas]] (legislature) of the [[Irish Free State]]. These [[Senate|Senator]]s were elected or appointed in 1922, and also elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Seanad election]].

==Composition of the 1925 Seanad==
The Free State Seanad was elected in stages and thus considered to be in permanent session. However, as a gesture of continuity with its Free State predecessor, the first [[Seanad Éireann|Seanad elected after 1937]] is numbered as the "Second Seanad". The Free State Senate, despite the occurrence of five senatorial elections before its abolition, is considered to have been a single 'Seanad' for the duration of its existence and is thus referred for that whole period as the "First Seanad".

There were a total of 60 seats in the Free State Seanad. 19 Senators were elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Free State Seanad election]], which was the only Seanad [[Universal suffrage|popular election]]. In 1922, 35 Senators had been elected by [[Dáil Éireann (Irish Free State)|Dáil Éireann]], and 25 had been nominated by the [[President of the Executive Council of the Irish Free State|President of the Executive Council]], [[W. T. Cosgrave]].

This is a list of the members of the '''1925 [[Seanad Éireann (Irish Free State)|Seanad Éireann]]''', the [[upper house]] of the [[Oireachtas of the Irish Free State|Oireachtas]] (legislature) of the [[Irish Free State]]. These [[Senate|Senator]]s were elected or appointed in 1922, and also elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Seanad election]].

==Composition of the 1925 Seanad==
The Free State Seanad was elected in stages and thus considered to be in permanent session. However, as a gesture of continuity with its Free State predecessor, the first [[Seanad Éireann|Seanad elected after 1937]] is numbered as the "Second Seanad". The Free State Senate, despite the occurrence of five senatorial elections before its abolition, is considered to have been a single 'Seanad' for the duration of its existence and is thus referred for that whole period as the "First Seanad".

There were a total of 60 seats in the Free State Seanad. 19 Senators were elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Free State Seanad election]], which was the only Seanad [[Universal suffrage|popular election]]. In 1922, 35 Senators had been elected by [[Dáil Éireann (Irish Free State)|Dáil Éireann]], and 25 had been nominated by the [[President of the Executive Council of the Irish Free State|President of the Executive Council]], [[W. T. Cosgrave]].

This is a list of the members of the '''1925 [[Seanad Éireann (Irish Free State)|Seanad Éireann]]''', the [[upper house]] of the [[Oireachtas of the Irish Free State|Oireachtas]] (legislature) of the [[Irish Free State]]. These [[Senate|Senator]]s were elected or appointed in 1922, and also elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Seanad election]].

==Composition of the 1925 Seanad==
The Free State Seanad was elected in stages and thus considered to be in permanent session. However, as a gesture of continuity with its Free State predecessor, the first [[Seanad Éireann|Seanad elected after 1937]] is numbered as the "Second Seanad". The Free State Senate, despite the occurrence of five senatorial elections before its abolition, is considered to have been a single 'Seanad' for the duration of its existence and is thus referred for that whole period as the "First Seanad".

There were a total of 60 seats in the Free State Seanad. 19 Senators were elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Free State Seanad election]], which was the only Seanad [[Universal suffrage|popular election]]. In 1922, 35 Senators had been elected by [[Dáil Éireann (Irish Free State)|Dáil Éireann]], and 25 had been nominated by the [[President of the Executive Council of the Irish Free State|President of the Executive Council]], [[W. T. Cosgrave]].

This is a list of the members of the '''1925 [[Seanad Éireann (Irish Free State)|Seanad Éireann]]''', the [[upper house]] of the [[Oireachtas of the Irish Free State|Oireachtas]] (legislature) of the [[Irish Free State]]. These [[Senate|Senator]]s were elected or appointed in 1922, and also elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Seanad election]].

==Composition of the 1925 Seanad==
The Free State Seanad was elected in stages and thus considered to be in permanent session. However, as a gesture of continuity with its Free State predecessor, the first [[Seanad Éireann|Seanad elected after 1937]] is numbered as the "Second Seanad". The Free State Senate, despite the occurrence of five senatorial elections before its abolition, is considered to have been a single 'Seanad' for the duration of its existence and is thus referred for that whole period as the "First Seanad".

There were a total of 60 seats in the Free State Seanad. 19 Senators were elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Free State Seanad election]], which was the only Seanad [[Universal suffrage|popular election]]. In 1922, 35 Senators had been elected by [[Dáil Éireann (Irish Free State)|Dáil Éireann]], and 25 had been nominated by the [[President of the Executive Council of the Irish Free State|President of the Executive Council]], [[W. T. Cosgrave]].

This is a list of the members of the '''1925 [[Seanad Éireann (Irish Free State)|Seanad Éireann]]''', the [[upper house]] of the [[Oireachtas of the Irish Free State|Oireachtas]] (legislature) of the [[Irish Free State]]. These [[Senate|Senator]]s were elected or appointed in 1922, and also elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Seanad election]].

==Composition of the 1925 Seanad==
The Free State Seanad was elected in stages and thus considered to be in permanent session. However, as a gesture of continuity with its Free State predecessor, the first [[Seanad Éireann|Seanad elected after 1937]] is numbered as the "Second Seanad". The Free State Senate, despite the occurrence of five senatorial elections before its abolition, is considered to have been a single 'Seanad' for the duration of its existence and is thus referred for that whole period as the "First Seanad".

There were a total of 60 seats in the Free State Seanad. 19 Senators were elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Free State Seanad election]], which was the only Seanad [[Universal suffrage|popular election]]. In 1922, 35 Senators had been elected by [[Dáil Éireann (Irish Free State)|Dáil Éireann]], and 25 had been nominated by the [[President of the Executive Council of the Irish Free State|President of the Executive Council]], [[W. T. Cosgrave]].

This is a list of the members of the '''1925 [[Seanad Éireann (Irish Free State)|Seanad Éireann]]''', the [[upper house]] of the [[Oireachtas of the Irish Free State|Oireachtas]] (legislature) of the [[Irish Free State]]. These [[Senate|Senator]]s were elected or appointed in 1922, and also elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Seanad election]].

==Composition of the 1925 Seanad==
The Free State Seanad was elected in stages and thus considered to be in permanent session. However, as a gesture of continuity with its Free State predecessor, the first [[Seanad Éireann|Seanad elected after 1937]] is numbered as the "Second Seanad". The Free State Senate, despite the occurrence of five senatorial elections before its abolition, is considered to have been a single 'Seanad' for the duration of its existence and is thus referred for that whole period as the "First Seanad".

There were a total of 60 seats in the Free State Seanad. 19 Senators were elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Free State Seanad election]], which was the only Seanad [[Universal suffrage|popular election]]. In 1922, 35 Senators had been elected by [[Dáil Éireann (Irish Free State)|Dáil Éireann]], and 25 had been nominated by the [[President of the Executive Council of the Irish Free State|President of the Executive Council]], [[W. T. Cosgrave]].

This is a list of the members of the '''1925 [[Seanad Éireann (Irish Free State)|Seanad Éireann]]''', the [[upper house]] of the [[Oireachtas of the Irish Free State|Oireachtas]] (legislature) of the [[Irish Free State]]. These [[Senate|Senator]]s were elected or appointed in 1922, and also elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Seanad election]].

==Composition of the 1925 Seanad==
The Free State Seanad was elected in stages and thus considered to be in permanent session. However, as a gesture of continuity with its Free State predecessor, the first [[Seanad Éireann|Seanad elected after 1937]] is numbered as the "Second Seanad". The Free State Senate, despite the occurrence of five senatorial elections before its abolition, is considered to have been a single 'Seanad' for the duration of its existence and is thus referred for that whole period as the "First Seanad".

There were a total of 60 seats in the Free State Seanad. 19 Senators were elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Free State Seanad election]], which was the only Seanad [[Universal suffrage|popular election]]. In 1922, 35 Senators had been elected by [[Dáil Éireann (Irish Free State)|Dáil Éireann]], and 25 had been nominated by the [[President of the Executive Council of the Irish Free State|President of the Executive Council]], [[W. T. Cosgrave]].

This is a list of the members of the '''1925 [[Seanad Éireann (Irish Free State)|Seanad Éireann]]''', the [[upper house]] of the [[Oireachtas of the Irish Free State|Oireachtas]] (legislature) of the [[Irish Free State]]. These [[Senate|Senator]]s were elected or appointed in 1922, and also elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Seanad election]].

==Composition of the 1925 Seanad==
The Free State Seanad was elected in stages and thus considered to be in permanent session. However, as a gesture of continuity with its Free State predecessor, the first [[Seanad Éireann|Seanad elected after 1937]] is numbered as the "Second Seanad". The Free State Senate, despite the occurrence of five senatorial elections before its abolition, is considered to have been a single 'Seanad' for the duration of its existence and is thus referred for that whole period as the "First Seanad".

There were a total of 60 seats in the Free State Seanad. 19 Senators were elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Free State Seanad election]], which was the only Seanad [[Universal suffrage|popular election]]. In 1922, 35 Senators had been elected by [[Dáil Éireann (Irish Free State)|Dáil Éireann]], and 25 had been nominated by the [[President of the Executive Council of the Irish Free State|President of the Executive Council]], [[W. T. Cosgrave]].

This is a list of the members of the '''1925 [[Seanad Éireann (Irish Free State)|Seanad Éireann]]''', the [[upper house]] of the [[Oireachtas of the Irish Free State|Oireachtas]] (legislature) of the [[Irish Free State]]. These [[Senate|Senator]]s were elected or appointed in 1922, and also elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Seanad election]].

==Composition of the 1925 Seanad==
The Free State Seanad was elected in stages and thus considered to be in permanent session. However, as a gesture of continuity with its Free State predecessor, the first [[Seanad Éireann|Seanad elected after 1937]] is numbered as the "Second Seanad". The Free State Senate, despite the occurrence of five senatorial elections before its abolition, is considered to have been a single 'Seanad' for the duration of its existence and is thus referred for that whole period as the "First Seanad".

There were a total of 60 seats in the Free State Seanad. 19 Senators were elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Free State Seanad election]], which was the only Seanad [[Universal suffrage|popular election]]. In 1922, 35 Senators had been elected by [[Dáil Éireann (Irish Free State)|Dáil Éireann]], and 25 had been nominated by the [[President of the Executive Council of the Irish Free State|President of the Executive Council]], [[W. T. Cosgrave]].

This is a list of the members of the '''1925 [[Seanad Éireann (Irish Free State)|Seanad Éireann]]''', the [[upper house]] of the [[Oireachtas of the Irish Free State|Oireachtas]] (legislature) of the [[Irish Free State]]. These [[Senate|Senator]]s were elected or appointed in 1922, and also elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Seanad election]].

==Composition of the 1925 Seanad==
The Free State Seanad was elected in stages and thus considered to be in permanent session. However, as a gesture of continuity with its Free State predecessor, the first [[Seanad Éireann|Seanad elected after 1937]] is numbered as the "Second Seanad". The Free State Senate, despite the occurrence of five senatorial elections before its abolition, is considered to have been a single 'Seanad' for the duration of its existence and is thus referred for that whole period as the "First Seanad".

There were a total of 60 seats in the Free State Seanad. 19 Senators were elected at the [[Irish Free State Seanad election, 1925|1925 Free State Seanad election]], which was the only Seanad [[Universal suffrage|popular election]]. In 1922, 35 Senators had been elected by [[Dáil Éireann (Irish Free State)|Dáil Éireann]], and 25 had been nominated by the [[President of the Executive Council of the Irish Free State|President of the Executive Council]], [[W. T. Cosgrave]].
